proof.text: Proof: take A and B to be the actual coordinate-ring colimits strictHenselizationRing of the indicated geometric points, with eA and eB the identity spectrum isomorphisms. By affine neighbourhood cofinality and Tag 04HX, these colimits are the strict henselizations of the local rings at the images of σ and τ. Their residue fields are the separable algebraic closures of the respective point residue fields inside Ω; they are henselian local rings with separably closed residue fields. The integral factorizations hσ and hτ identify k and k' as algebraic extensions of those point residue fields. Since k and k' are separably closed, their embeddings into Ω contain these separable closures. The remaining extensions are algebraic purely inseparable: an algebraic extension of a separably closed field has no nontrivial separable part. Take ρA and ρB to be the spectra of these residue inclusions. Purely inseparable algebraic field extensions give integral, radicial, surjective spectrum maps, hence universal homeomorphisms. The inclusions extend the given point residue maps, so composition with the ring residue maps and the colimit structural maps gives σ and τ. No ring data are chosen from a mere unproved existence assertion.

theorem Etale.exists_compatibleStrictHenselizationCoreExistence
    {S T : Scheme.{u}} {g : T ⟶ S}
    {k k' Ω : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] [Field k'] [IsSepClosed k']
    [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (σ : Spec (.of k) ⟶ S) (τ : Spec (.of k') ⟶ T)
    (ι : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (hι : ι ≫ σ = τ ≫ g)
    (hσ : ∃ (s : S) (ψ : S.residueField s ⟶ .of k),
      ψ.hom.IsIntegral ∧ Spec.map ψ ≫ S.fromSpecResidueField s = σ)
    (hτ : ∃ (t : T) (ψ : T.residueField t ⟶ .of k'),
      ψ.hom.IsIntegral ∧ Spec.map ψ ≫ T.fromSpecResidueField t = τ)
    (ν : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec (.of k')) :
    let s := ν ≫ ι ≫ σ
    let t := ν ≫ τ
    ∃ (A B : Type u) (cA : CommRing A) (cB : CommRing B),
      letI := cA
      letI := cB
      ∃ (hA : HenselianLocalRing A) (hB : HenselianLocalRing B),
        letI := hA
        letI := hB
        ∃ (sA : IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A))
          (sB : IsSepClosed (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)),
          letI := sA
          letI := sB
          ∃ (eA : Spec (.of A) ≅ strictHenselizationScheme s)
            (eB : Spec (.of B) ≅ strictHenselizationScheme t)
            (ρA : Spec (.of k) ⟶ Spec (.of (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)))
            (ρB : Spec (.of k') ⟶ Spec (.of (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B))),
            IsUniversalHomeomorphism ρA ∧ IsUniversalHomeomorphism ρB ∧
            ρA ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue A)) ≫
              eA.hom ≫ strictHenselizationStructuralMap s = σ ∧
            ρB ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IsLocalRing.residue B)) ≫
              eB.hom ≫ strictHenselizationStructuralMap t = τ

statement: For the two geometric points induced from σ and τ in the algebraically closed Ω, the coordinate-ring strict henselizations have henselian local and separably closed residue structures, spectrum identifications, and universal-homeomorphism residue maps factoring σ and τ. No ring map between the two rings is asserted.
